lookup_tb_ptr.hand_justification: The mechanical reader refuses this helper because tb_lookup() reaches tb_lookup_cmp(), which calls get_page_addr_code(desc->env, virt_page1) -- an INSTRUCTION FETCH address translation on the hash-table miss path (accel/tcg/cpu-exec.c tb_lookup_cmp).  The row below states the only CPUArchState access on the path that returns: cpu_get_tb_cpu_state(env, &pc, &cs_base, &flags) at ../target/i386/cpu.h:2630, whose read set is derived by the same reader and is listed here verbatim.  It writes nothing: no member appears on the left of an assignment in that function.  The fetch is not in the model on any instruction -- no instruction records reading its own encoding -- so leaving it out is the same treatment every other instruction already gets, not an exception made for this one. Every field below is marked DF_HF_XLAT: these are the members cpu_get_tb_cpu_state() reads to compute the TB LOOKUP KEY, not operands of the guest instruction that chained.  They are enumerated so the row accounts for the whole footprint, and not published, because a `ret` does not depend on the vector type register.

raise_exception.hand_justification: R7.6: the state an instruction's EXCEPTION writes is in that instruction's destination set.  The mechanical reader cannot reach it because the write is not in the helper's body and not on any path the helper RETURNS from: helper_raise_exception() sets cs->exception_index and env->error_code and then calls cpu_loop_exit_restore() (../target/mips/tcg/exception.c:163-166), which longjmps out; the CP0 state is written afterwards by mips_cpu_do_interrupt() during exception DELIVERY.  EXCP_SYSCALL (../target/mips/tcg/system/tlb_helper.c:1354) and EXCP_TRAP (:1376) both `goto set_EPC`, and the set_EPC path is the source for every field below, cited per field.  BOTH fields carry REG_SYSEXC, which is the generic word the wire's destination slot for `syscall` and `teq` already names -- the row makes QEMU's list carry what the wire has been publishing, it does not add a destination the wire lacks.  NOT ENUMERATED, and each for a stated reason: env->CP0_EPC is written at :1423 but the tracer's register vocabulary has no row spelling `epc`, so naming it would produce a name that resolves to nothing (it is the same REG_SYSEXC either way, so nothing is lost by the omission); env->CP0_BadVAddr is NOT written on this path at all -- set_EPC only READS it (:1479, :1500, in the TLB cases), and the address exceptions that do write it arrive by a different route than a raise_exception call; env->hflags and env->active_tc.PC are written by delivery (:1440, :1443, and :1445/:1449/:1451/:1454) and are QEMU's own control-flow bookkeeping for the handler entry, not architectural destinations of the raising instruction -- R2 and J2.3, the same discriminator R10.1 applies to the block-final pc write.  The set below is therefore what the source states AND the vocabulary can name, and nothing else.  DIRECTION CORRECTED 2026-08-27: both fields are 3 (READ-MODIFY-WRITE), not 2 (write).  The citations above were always read-modify-writes and the row understated them.  CP0_Status is READ twice before it is written -- `if (!(env->CP0_Status & (1 << CP0St_EXL)))` is the gate on the whole set_EPC body (:1418) and Status.BEV selects the vector (:1445/:1449) -- and the write is `env->CP0_Status |= 1 << CP0St_EXL` (:1432), which reads it a third time.  CP0_Cause is read by every one of its three writes: the BD bit is a qatomic_or/qatomic_and (:1428/:1430) and the exception code goes through mips_cause_set_field (:1456), a cmpxchg loop over the whole word (../target/mips/internal.h:172).  R7 is the reason this matters rather than being a pedantic label: a read-modify-write MAKES THE OLD VALUE A SOURCE, so the destination's provenance names REG_SYSEXC instead of being empty -- and an empty provenance on a published destination is what dst_precheck() refuses, taking the whole destination family of the raising instruction with it.  Measured on `neg` (a TRAPPING `sub`, whose other destination is an ordinary GPR): with dir=2 the refusal deleted that GPR's published mask and the instruction's whole dep block.  Stating the read that the source performs is both the true fact and the fix.
